findings.problem: Visit-time native name/version contracts are computed from the full validated person and then discarded. The spool writes a lossy {localId, promptVersion, preferredNameSuggestion, identity-predicate claims} record and streamIdentityDossierIndex later calls localNameKeys/memberContract on that projection. Production corpus persons also carry book, chapter, mentions, descriptorSuggestion, remaining extraction fields, and non-identity claims; dropping them can change names, member versions, posting keys, and dossier bytes versus the baseline in-memory index. The new self-test never uses production-shaped persons (no book/chapter; mentions are ignoredByIdentity-only) and cannot prove exact name/version/index identity.
findings.requiredFix: Pin the contract taken from the full validated person: persist memberContract including names (and every field localNameKeys actually reads, including book/chapter/mentions if the native key reader uses them). Index from those pinned names/claims instead of recomputing keys from a reduced JSON person.

findings.problem: Scratch spool ${out}.members is created with mkdirSync({recursive:false}) and is intentionally left behind on validation/build failure, but out is only created later. existsSync(out) therefore does not guard retries. A failed run releases the lock, leaves an unpublished .members directory, and the next attempt at the same out throws a raw EEXIST from mkdir instead of the generation-reuse error used for out. That is a recovery regression versus baseline, where a corpus/index failure before writeIdentityDossierStore allowed retrying the same out. writer.close() also closes without flush, so the retained spool can omit up to 64KiB of pending member rows.
findings.requiredFix: Treat ${out}.members as an unpublished generation: if it already exists, throw the same class of explicit reuse/remove error used for out (do not depend on mkdir EEXIST). Flush pending bytes before close on the failure path so a retained spool actually contains the members already accepted. Keep the current rule that only a successful published registry deletes the spool.

reason: Streaming the production validator and writing dossiers from a generator preserves duplicate-id/source-chapter gates, posting-sort-after-all-clusters ordering, and coverage-before-manifest publication if the member records are faithful. They are not: the indexer consumes a reduced person, not the visit-time full-person memberContract, so exact native names/versions are not guaranteed despite byte-identical fixture tests. Retry/recovery of an unpublished generation is also newly blocked by a sibling .members directory.
